newsitem.title: USA: Monsanto files counterclain in Pioneer suit.
newsitem.headline: Monsanto files counterclain in Pioneer suit.

text.p: Monsanto Co said Friday it filed an answer and counterclaim in federal court in Madison, Wis., to a contract lawsuit initiated by Pioneer Hi-Bred International Inc in late March.

In its filing, Monsanto asked the court to terminate an agreement that gave Pioneer access to certain rights to biotechnology crop traits, specifically corn with bacillus thuringensis gene (Bt) that is protected against the European corn borer.
Access to this technology was originally granted in a 1993 license agreement between Monsanto and Pioneer, it added.
Monsanto also requested that the lawsuit be transferred to St. Louis.

"Monsanto indicated at the outset of this litigation that Pioneer's claim was totally without merit," David Snively, litigation counsel for Monsanto, said in a statement. "The actions taken by Pioneer breach our agreement and violate the basic tenets of our relationship," he alleged.
Snively added that Monsanto has asked the court to dismiss Pioneer's suit and declare that Monsanto's obligations toward Pioneer are terminated.
Pioneer was not immediately available for comment.
Monsanto said that Pioneer's lawsuit had asserted that Monsanto was obligated to obtain, for Pioneer's benefit, access to patent rights held by DeKalb Genetics Corp .

Monsanto said it is an investor in DeKalb and does not control DeKalb's technology. Monsanto added it believes it is not required under its original agreement with Pioneer to obtain freedom to operate for Pioneer from patent rights held by independent parties such as DeKalb.
Monsanto also said that Pioneer's lawsuit had claimed that Monsanto was engaged in a joint venture with Pioneer to develop Bt corn.

Monsanto said it denies that such a joint venture exists and that the development plan for Bt corn with Pioneer did not include undertaking to secure freedom for Pioneer from patent rights held by others.
Monsanto said its counterclaim alleges that Pioneer breached aspects of the 1993 agreement and allegedly failed to pay Monsanto a milestone payment of $10 million.
